provision_review.why: 15-30-3328 grants a refundable pass-through-entity credit against the chapter's taxes, and 15-62-208 imposes a separate recapture tax on individuals. Both change a resident's net Montana liability. The pre-fix mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies gate has no conjunct or hold for either one, so it admits those taxpayers and reports a net liability that leaves them out. The post-fix gate excludes them through explicit applicability facts.
provision_review.adjudication_note: Both readers give the same verdict and both quote 15-30-3328 and 15-62-208. Reader A adds 15-30-2328 (other/006). It is valid but not needed, and the two shortest files the post-fix gate's proof atoms cite carry the point. 019 (1,070 chars) and 022 (2,825 chars) are short enough to fit the judge window together. Both quotes check against the files.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module returned a full-year-resident net liability that silently omitted clauses the cited Montana statutes state: the separate lump-sum/farm-ranch/recapture taxes and credit recoveries under 15-30-2105, 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 53-25-118, 15-30-2328(3) and 15-30-2359(6) and the refundable 15-30-3328 pass-through-entity credit had no representation at all, the 15-30-2120(5)(a) family-education deduction was parked as a typed hold even though its $4,500/$9,000 caps and account-owner relationship test are in the pinned corpus, and the adoption credit multiplied per-adoption amounts by unbounded counts with none of 15-30-2321's eligible-child (under 18 or incapable of self-care), adoption-final-in-year, or "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child" conditions.
triage.triage_notes: Single module file, but this is a multi-defect review-fix commit; at least four distinct fidelity corrections land in the same diff and I had to pick one kind. (1) unrepresented_clause, the dominant pattern: missing separate taxes/recaptures and the PTE credit (now fail-closed applicability holds in mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies), the missing 15-30-2120(5)(a) family-education deduction (new caps 4500/9000, child/stepchild Montana-residency test, added into mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_subtractions and the corresponding hold input mt_pit_2026_has_family_education_contribution_deduction deleted), and the missing 15-30-2321 eligible-child/one-credit conditions on mt_pit_2026_refundable_adoption_credit. (2) untraceable_branch: the pre-fix mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_montana_taxable_income wrapped fed TI + additions - subtractions in max(0, ...) with no basis in 15-30-2101; the fix renames it to mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_signed_section_2101_amount without the floor and introduces mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_schedule_tax_base = max(0, ...) so only the 15-30-2103 schedule base is floored (module summary: "computes Montana taxable income without forcing a nonnegative floor, floors only the schedule base"). (3) polarity_or_logic / fail-open: the refundable adoption, EITC, and public-access credit rules previously computed unconditionally and now return 0 when mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies is false (PR body: "transitive fail-closed gates"). (4) capital character: a new gate requires section_1222_net_long_term_capital_gain == 0 or both additions and subtractions == 0, because Montana modifications can change income character. Also in scope but not a defect: the public-access hold was renamed and NARROWED (mt_pit_2026_has_shared_or_duplicate_public_access_claim -> mt_pit_2026_has_shared_ownership_or_same_property_public_access_allocation, so separate properties under 15-30-2380(4) no longer set the hold), and ~25 cross-title modification inputs gained `== 0` requirements in the profile gate (PR body finding "caller-completed legal results"). Provisions read through the pinned release: MCA 15-30-2120(5)(a) confirms the $4,500/$9,000 caps, the taxpayer/spouse/child-or-stepchild account-owner constraint with the Montana-residency condition, and (5)(b) the 15-62-208 recapture tax; MCA 15-30-2321 confirms the $7,500/$5,000 amounts, subsection (5) "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child." and subsection (7) "eligible child" = under 18 or incapable of self-care. MCA 15-30-2105 could NOT be resolved: the resolver reported "Active corpus source 'us-mt/statute/15-30-2105' is repealed" for every candidate release, so the lump-sum-distribution excerpt is taken from the module's own proof atom, not independently verified. Commit message body is empty; PR body is the best commit-level evidence ("Findings covering specialty taxes and recaptures, capital character, transitive fail-closed gates, caller-completed legal results, public-output gating, federal-EITC domain consistency, adoption proof completeness, and generated-artifact minimality were fixed and revalidated."). Follow-up: 915fc7cc8 "Tighten Montana resident core domain" touches this same module after this commit; a PR comment says that rebase carried no substantive Montana changes, so reviewers should check whether 915fc7cc8 contains further fidelity fixes. Companion test file changed by +3,181 lines in the same commit.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module (34b60479:us-mt/.../resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml, rule mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies, lines 414-465) emitted mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_net_income_tax_liability = "Net Montana income-tax liability before payments" for a gate that had no conjunct, input, or hold for the separate taxes and recaptures MCA 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 15-30-2328(3), 15-30-2359(6) and 15-30-2120(6)(b)/53-25-118 impose, or for the refundable 15-30-3328 pass-through-entity credit, so a resident with any of them silently got an understated liability; the fix adds the raw facts and gate conjuncts, i.e. it adds representation of clauses the source states. I read those provisions in the release the commit's toolchain pins (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current) and every added proof excerpt is verbatim in the corpus body ("There is a recapture tax at a rate equal to the highest rate of tax provided in 15-30-2103"; "increase the amount of tax due under 15-30-2103 or 15-31-101 by the amount of the credit allowed"; "may claim the distributive share of the owner's entity tax paid by an electing pass-through entity as a refundable credit"). The "new coverage it never claimed" defense fails because the pre-fix gate affirmatively admitted those taxpayers, and it also fails for the family-education deduction: the pre-fix hold rationale called it "indexed", but 15-30-2120(7)(a) indexes only subsections (3)(g) and (3)(o), so the fixed $4,500/$9,000 caps in (5)(a) were a source-stated deduction left unrepresented. The one weak item is 15-30-2105, which the pinned corpus row marks metadata.status "repealed".

triage.verifier_notes: Reviewer caveats. (1) Multi-defect commit: besides the quoted unrepresented clauses it also (a) rewrites the refundable adoption credit from an ungated count product (`mt_pit_2026_foster_care_adoption_amount * ..._count + ...`) to a single child-level claim conditioned on 15-30-2321's "eligible child" age-18/self-care test, 2026 finality and "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child." (all three excerpts verified verbatim) — also unrepresented_clause; (b) gates mt_pit_2026_refundable_earned_income_credit and mt_pit_2026_refundable_public_access_credit on the profile, which is a fail-open→fail-closed fix (polarity_or_logic); (c) splits mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_montana_taxable_income into a signed 15-30-2101 amount plus a floored 15-30-2103 schedule base, removing an ungrounded max(0) on Montana taxable income (arguably untraceable_branch). If the corpus wants one kind per case, unrepresented_clause is the dominant and the one the quoted comment supports; wrong_entity_or_scope is an adjacent reading (the supported population was too broad) but the cause is the missing clauses. (2) Partial weakness in the first reader's quote: MCA 15-30-2105 (lump-sum distribution tax) carries metadata.status "repealed" in the pinned release row (656 of the MT Title-15 rows carry that status, so the flag is meaningful), and `resolve_provision.py` refuses it as "Active corpus source ... is repealed" — the lump-sum hold added for it is conservative rather than source-required. The other six items are active sections and carry the fidelity finding on their own. (3) Provenance: this is a review-fix commit inside PR #1031, the PR that first introduced the module, so the defective state never reached main; that is a corpus-curation question (does the corpus admit intra-PR fixes?), not a classification one. (4) Verified read-only via git show, the scratchpad release JSONL, and resolve_provision.py; no repo state touched.
